takeaways: Mortgage rates are back above 7%. Jason cites Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed average of 7.28% as of October 1, 2026, up from 6.34% a year earlier.
The Federal Reserve doesn't set mortgage rates. They follow the 10-year Treasury yield, and your own rate also depends on your credit, down payment, loan type and points.

On a $415,000 Dakota County home with 20% down (a loan of about $332,000), principal and interest rise from about $2,064 a month at 6.34% to about $2,272 at 7.28%: about $208 more a month, close to $2,500 a year.
Fannie Mae's September forecast, as quoted in the video, has rates around 6.8% for the rest of 2026 and 6.7% for 2027, so waiting for much lower rates could take more than a year.

Homes are still selling: in Dakota County in August, closed sales were up over 7%, the median price rose almost 4%, homes averaged about 43 days on market and sellers got about 98% of their original list price.

Assumable FHA and VA loans let a buyer take over the seller's lower rate. The buyer must cover the gap between the price and the loan balance with cash or a second loan, and assumptions usually take 45 days or more.
Sellers with a low-rate FHA or VA loan should advertise that it's assumable, and price carefully, since higher rates mean fewer buyers qualify.

faq.q: Does the Federal Reserve set mortgage rates?
faq.a: No. Mortgage rates follow the 10-year Treasury yield, which the bond market trades every day. Your own rate also depends on your credit, down payment, loan type and any points you pay.

faq.q: Can someone who isn't a veteran assume a VA loan?
faq.a: Yes. A non-veteran can assume a VA loan, but the seller's VA entitlement may stay tied to that loan until it's paid off, so sellers should understand that before agreeing.

faq.q: How much does a higher mortgage rate add to a monthly payment?
faq.a: In Jason's example, a loan of about $332,000 costs about $2,064 a month in principal and interest at 6.34% and about $2,272 at 7.28%, roughly $208 more a month before taxes, insurance and association dues.
